task.description: Hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's amendment (new S2.5 section) to lib/letflow/design/req372-semantic-decision-rule-validation.md, per WF-02 Step 1b's same procedure applied to this amendment. You are on branch feature/WF02-REQ372-20260921 -- verify with git branch --show-current, pull if needed. Read the amended design section directly. Verify: (1) the empty-declared_fields behavior (skip both violation classes, return {valid: true, violations: []}) is stated explicitly with real reasoning, not asserted; (2) the amendment's own claim that all 10 original acceptance criteria remain unaffected is actually verified -- re-check AC1-AC6 yourself against the actual test scenarios TEST-DESIGNER wrote (test/specs/REQ-372.md and the two test files) to confirm none of them exercises the definition with an EMPTY declared_fields map in a way that would now silently pass when it should still fail; (3) no implementation code (function bodies) was introduced by the amendment -- signature/behavior description only; (4) the fix genuinely resolves the diagnosed root cause without requiring any pre-existing fixture to be modified -- read handoffs/WF02-REQ372-20260921/step-03-test-designer.json's failure evidence and confirm the amendment's mechanism (guard inside validate/2 itself, applying uniformly to both call sites) actually closes that gap by construction. FAIL immediately on any check failure.
acceptance_criteria: empty-declared_fields behavior stated explicitly with reasoning
AC1-AC6 compatibility independently re-verified against the actual test scenarios, not just CODE-DESIGNER's own claim
no implementation code introduced by the amendment
the amendment's mechanism plausibly closes the 31-fixture regression without requiring fixture edits

result.summary:
Checks 1, 3, and 4 pass: the empty-declared_fields decision (skip both violation classes, return {valid: true, violations: []} unconditionally when declared_fields == %{}) is stated explicitly with real reasoning in new S2.5 of lib/letflow/design/req372-semantic-decision-rule-validation.md (S2.5.1/S2.5.2), no implementation code (function bodies) was introduced -- only @spec-level signature/behavior description changed for validate/2, and the guard's placement inside validate/2 itself (S2.5.3), applying uniformly to both activate/2 and validate_definition_graph/2 call sites with no per-caller special-casing, plausibly closes the 31-fixture regression from step-03-test-designer.json's evidence without requiring any of those fixtures to be edited (none of them ever seed a variable_schemas row, so declared_fields is %{} for all of them and the new guard applies by construction).

Check 2 FAILS. The amendment's S2.5.4 claims 'AC1-AC6 all describe definitions with real, non-empty declared fields, so the new empty-declared_fields branch is simply never reached by any of their test cases.' This is false -- independently re-checked against the actual committed test files (test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_test.exs, test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_activation_test.exs, both listed in step-03-test-designer.json's artifacts_out and already committed/pushed) and found THREE test scenarios that call validate/2 (directly or via activate/2 / validate_definition_graph/2) with an EMPTY declared_fields map and assert a violation IS produced -- exactly the case the amendment's guard now silently short-circuits to zero violations: (1) test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_test.exs:106-113, 'with zero declared fields, no suggestion clause is emitted at all' -- calls SemanticValidation.validate(graph, %{}) then does `[message] = messages(result)`, expecting exactly one violation message (the test's actual intent is to check the SUGGESTION CLAUSE is omitted, not that no violation occurs at all); under the amendment this becomes `[message] = []`, a MatchError. (2) test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_activation_test.exs:211-231, the 'reverse' AC6 test ('variable_schemas starts undeclared, is seeded afterward') -- creates a definition with zero variable_schemas rows seeded, asserts `{:ok, %{valid: false, violations: violations}} = Definitions.validate_definition_graph(...)` and `Enum.any?(violations, &(&1.code == :undeclared_variable_reference))`; under the amendment this now returns `{:ok, %{valid: true, violations: []}}` -- both assertions fail. (3) test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_activation_test.exs:241-259, 'a declared_fields/condition mismatch reports via the read-only endpoint' -- same pattern, an unseeded (empty-declared_fields) definition asserted to produce a valid: false result with an :undeclared_variable_reference violation via validate_definition_graph/2 directly; same failure mode. These three tests are not part of the 31-fixture regression (they are REQ-372's OWN new tests, deliberately exercising the pre-amendment behavior where field-existence fires even against an empty declared_fields map), but they are real, already-committed, currently-passing-in-isolation tests (step-03-test-designer.json's result.summary confirms 'test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_test.exs ... all pass in isolation' and 'test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_activation_test.exs ... all pass in isolation') that this amendment, exactly as specified, would newly break. The amendment does not acknowledge, address, or resolve this -- it neither revises these three tests' expectations nor narrows its own exemption to avoid the conflict. This is precisely the check the triggering handoff's task instruction (point 2) asked to verify was NOT true ('confirm none of them exercises the definition with an EMPTY declared_fields map in a way that would now silently pass when it should still fail') -- three of them do exactly that.

issues.description: The S2.5 amendment's empty-declared_fields short-circuit (validate/2 returns {valid: true, violations: []} unconditionally whenever declared_fields == %{}) conflicts with three test scenarios TEST-DESIGNER already wrote and committed, all of which deliberately construct an empty-declared_fields definition and assert a real violation is produced. Fix requires either: (a) narrowing the amendment so the empty-declared_fields exemption applies only at the activate/2 and validate_definition_graph/2 call sites for definitions that were never intended to be schema-checked (distinguishing that from these tests' intent), which the current guard-inside-validate/2-itself placement (S2.5.3) does not allow since it's unconditional and caller-agnostic; or (b) explicitly revising the three named test expectations as part of this amendment (with reasoning for why their original empty-declared_fields assertions were wrong) and stating that revision in the design doc; or (c) some other explicit reconciliation. The amendment currently does none of these -- it asserts compatibility that isn't actually true against the committed tests.
issues.evidence: test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_test.exs:106-113; test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_activation_test.exs:211-231 and :241-259; each cited with exact line numbers and assertion text in result.summary above.

result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER -- resolve the conflict between S2.5's empty-declared_fields exemption and the three committed test scenarios (test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_test.exs:106-113, test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_activation_test.exs:211-231 and :241-259) that assert a violation for an empty declared_fields definition. The amendment must either change its own mechanism so those scenarios keep failing as originally intended, or explicitly revise those test expectations (routed to TEST-DESIGNER) with stated reasoning, before this design amendment can be regated.
